subject: Data description and representation
notes: Stem: `OK  §8.5.4` "A zero-length item is a data item or a literal whose minimum length is zero and whose length at runtime is zero." The compiler holds the stem's description half as ONE recurrence (DataItem.MinimumLengthIsZero) and the runtime half as the emitted current-length test; consumers read it (MoveClassifier.ZeroLengthItemRoute / MoveEmitter for §14.9.25.4 GR1, CobolClass for §8.8.4.4.4 GR1, STRING/UNSTRING/INSPECT runtime length). Item 7: MinimumOccurrences is 0 for an OccursSpec.IsDynamic table, so a group of only dynamic-capacity tables answers yes. Probe p2: `01 VG. 05 VT PIC X OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN VC.` -> FUNCTION LENGTH(VG)=0. VG is a variable-length group (§8.5.1.12.1 `Unlike other group items, a variable-length group is not equivalent to an alphanumeric data item`), so class condition / UNSTRING / INSPECT refuse it by their own SRs and MOVE/compare are GR9 / §8.8.4.2.17 compatible-group operations (MoveClassifier's recorded determination that GR9 governs). STRING's identifier-1 under-reject of VG is recorded in dossier_gaps. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 2014, 2023 (dynamic-capacity tables are a post-2002 facility). §8.5.4 is not in Annex E's 2014->2023 delta, so the concept predates 2023; the repo holds no 2002/2014 text, so the 2002-vs-2014 introduction edge is not separately derivable (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE ratified decision #1).
